data.content_ref: inline:The mechanism's concluding sentence — 'It follows that the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all' — is a non-sequitur that directly contradicts the claim's own framing. The claim explicitly posits verisimilitude (truth-likeness) as the coherent target of the critical selection mechanism, which makes the theory's relation to truth ('underlying structure') the entire point of the preference. If the underlying structure (i.e., the theory's actual proximity to truth) were 'never relevant to the outcome,' then verisimilitude cannot function as the target the mechanism claims to optimize, and the distinction between 'gamble on severity' and 'probability of success' collapses into meaninglessness — there would be nothing the gamble is gambling toward. The sentence provides no derivation step connecting the asymmetry-of-falsification reasoning to this conclusion, and it is not licensed by any of the listed counterconditions or premises. This is a substantive internal inconsistency: the mechanism asserts the irrelevance of the very thing the claim says is at stake.
